title: Databases Practice Exam
description: Practice SQLite basics, SQL parameters, and storing app data in tables.

questions.prompt: Which module is built into Python for SQLite databases?
questions.explanation: import sqlite3 connects to .db files without installing extra packages.

questions.prompt: What does conn.execute("SELECT * FROM todos") return?
options: A cursor you can fetch rows from
questions.explanation: execute runs SQL; fetchone/fetchall read result rows from the cursor.

questions.prompt: Using ? placeholders in SQL helps prevent SQL injection when passing user input.
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries keep values separate from the SQL text.

questions.prompt: conn.commit() is needed after INSERT because:
options: Changes are not saved permanently until you commit
questions.explanation: SQLite uses transactions; commit writes pending changes to the database file.

questions.prompt: A PRIMARY KEY column in a table:
questions.explanation: Primary keys give each row a stable unique id.

questions.prompt: What file extension is common for a SQLite database on disk?
questions.explanation: SQLite stores data in a single file such as todos.db.

questions.prompt: SQLite is a good fit for learning and small local apps.
questions.explanation: It is serverless, file-based, and ships with Python.

questions.prompt: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS todos (...) means:
options: Create the table only when it does not already exist
Insert a row named IF NOT EXISTS
questions.explanation: IF NOT EXISTS avoids errors when setup runs more than once.

questions.prompt: cursor.fetchall() returns:
options: A list of row tuples from the query
questions.explanation: fetchall reads every remaining row from the last SELECT.

questions.prompt: Why use with sqlite3.connect() as conn?
options: The connection closes reliably when the block ends
questions.explanation: Context managers ensure cleanup even if an error occurs.

questions.prompt: SQLAlchemy is mainly used to:
options: Work with databases using Python classes and an ORM layer
questions.explanation: ORMs map tables to Python objects for common database tasks.

questions.prompt: An ORM can generate SQL while you work with Python objects.
questions.explanation: SQLAlchemy builds queries from model definitions and sessions.

questions.prompt: INSERT INTO todos (text, done) VALUES (?, ?) adds:
options: One new row with those column values
questions.explanation: INSERT adds data; placeholders bind Python values safely.

questions.prompt: SELECT id, text FROM todos WHERE done = 0 returns:
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before they are returned.

questions.prompt: Compared to a JSON file, a database helps when you need:
questions.explanation: SQL queries filter, sort, and update specific rows efficiently.

questions.prompt: You should commit after writes in sqlite3 unless autocommit mode is on.
questions.explanation: Without commit, changes may not persist when the connection closes.

questions.prompt: A database schema describes:
questions.explanation: Schema is the structure of your tables.

questions.prompt: list_todos() style helpers in a project:
options: Keep SQL in one place separate from menu code
questions.explanation: Data-access functions are easier to test and reuse.

questions.prompt: SQLAlchemy is installed with:
questions.explanation: sqlite3 is stdlib; SQLAlchemy is a third-party package.

questions.prompt: Foreign keys can link rows in one table to rows in another.
questions.explanation: Relationships model real-world links between entities.
